$comment: Structural rules Stripe documents about the Sigma schema. build_schema.py applies these to synthesize whole table families (metadata, Connect mirrors) so they don't have to be hand-listed. Each rule cites the doc page that states it.

metadata_tables.rule: Every object table with user-settable metadata has a sibling table named <table>_metadata. Each row is one key/value pair, joined back to the parent by a foreign key named <singular_object>_id.

columns.name: <parent>_id
columns.description: References the id column of the parent object table.

columns.name: key
columns.description: The metadata key set on the object.

columns.name: value
columns.description: The metadata value for that key. Always a string, even when it holds a number or boolean.

metadata_tables.grain: One row per (object, metadata key) pair. Objects with no metadata have no rows.
metadata_tables.quote: The metadata table contains a foreign key to the corresponding object in the primary table that you can use to join the two tables. For example, every row in the issuing_transactions_metadata table has the column issuing_transaction_id that references the id column of a row in the issuing_transactions table.
metadata_tables.pivot_recipe: select parent_id, map_agg(key, value) as md from <table>_metadata group by 1 -- then md['your_key']

connect_mirror_tables.rule: Connect platforms get a parallel table for connected-account data, named connected_account_<base table>. It carries the same columns as the base table plus an `account` column holding the connected account id.

extra_columns.name: account
extra_columns.description: The connected account (acct_...) this row belongs to.

connect_mirror_tables.quote: Each Connect-specific table has an additional `account` column containing the identifier of a connected account.
connect_mirror_tables.caveat: Which base tables have a connected_account_ mirror varies by account and by product enablement. Only mirrors that Stripe documents or that you have verified are listed as tables here.

id_prefixes.$comment: Stripe object ids are prefixed by type. Useful for sanity-checking a join and for recognizing what a polymorphic source_id points at.

api_to_sigma_divergence.$comment: Sigma column names follow API conventions but are NOT mechanically derivable from the API object. Measured against the documented `charges` columns, naive derivation from the OpenAPI spec missed 21 real columns and invented 17 that don't exist. These are the observed rules. Treat them as heuristics for guessing a name to verify, never as proof a column exists.

rules.rule: Nested objects are flattened with underscores.
Some nested prefixes are dropped entirely when unambiguous.
Some booleans are exposed as timestamps instead.
The API `object` discriminator field is not present in Sigma.
Deeply nested arrays become their own tables rather than columns.

data_load_time.description: Not a column — a query-scoped constant available in every Sigma query, holding the time through which your account's data is complete. Use it instead of current_date to make scheduled queries deterministic.
data_load_time.example: where created >= data_load_time - interval '1' month and created < data_load_time

amount_units.default: Amounts are integers in the currency's smallest unit (cents for USD, yen for JPY). An amount of 1000 with currency usd is 10.00 USD.

exceptions.note: amount and tax on these tables are in MAJOR currency units, not minor units. Do not divide by 100.
